strengths: Comprehensive and large-scale empirical study with 2,347 math problems, 1,196 QA problems, and 901 NL reasoning problems across 14 models and multiple domains

Novel finding that verifier generation capability exhibits difficulty-dependent non-linear correlation (saturated for easy, linear for medium, threshold-limited for hard), extending beyond prior linear characterizations
Demonstrates practical impact showing weak generators can match strong generator post-verification performance (75.5% gap reduction), with clear guidance on when strong verifiers provide no advantage
Rigorous experimental design with model-agnostic difficulty definition, careful handling of edge cases, multiple verification methods for ground truth, and analyses at multiple granularities
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and comprehensive appendices including prompt templates, case studies, and reasoning model analysis supporting reproducibility
Identifies fundamental verification limitations that verifier scaling alone cannot overcome, with important practical implications for cost-effective TTS deployment
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty—primarily an empirical characterization study without new verification methods, training approaches, or theoretical frameworks; many findings are somewhat expected given prior knowledge of verification asymmetry

Restrictive scope with significant limitations: uses same model for generator and verifier (limited cross-model exploration), covers only 3 domains (math, QA, NL reasoning), excludes code generation and open-ended tasks, and only explores reference-free verification

Incomplete mechanistic understanding—case studies are illustrative but limited in depth; root causes of verification asymmetry are demonstrated but not deeply investigated; phase-transition behavior in verifier capability lacks theoretical grounding

Lacks statistical rigor—no confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty quantification reported; strong claims ('bottleneck is not model capacity') lack formal statistical validation; only single 64-sample per model-problem pair

Reasoning model analysis underdeveloped—only two reasoning models examined; the finding that TNR shows different difficulty-dependence for reasoning vs. instruction-tuned models deserves deeper investigation but is relegated to appendix

Problem filtering for RQ2 excludes some problems; unclear how much data is lost and whether this introduces selection bias; experimental choices (greedy decoding, corner case handling) could affect results without sensitivity analysis

strengths: Comprehensive empirical study across 4,444 problems, 14 models, 3 domains with well-controlled experiments and proper stratification
Identifies non-linear correlation regimes (saturated/linear/threshold-limited) between verifier capability and performance that extends prior linear understanding
Strong interpretability analysis with quantitative evidence for hypothesized mechanisms (Figures 3, 5) and illuminating case studies
Practical findings demonstrating weak generators can close 75.7% performance gap with strong ones and identifying regimes where verifier scaling provides no benefit
Extensive validation across domains, reasoning models, different prompts, and large models (Qwen3-235B) demonstrating robustness
Rigorous experimental design with multiple difficulty measures (oracle and practical) and careful handling of evaluation imbalances
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: individual findings are somewhat intuitive (problem difficulty affects TPR, strong generators produce harder-to-detect errors, verifier capability correlates with performance); contribution is primarily systematic characterization rather than new insights

Narrow evaluation scope: limited to verifiable problems with objective ground-truth; excludes subjective reasoning, open-ended tasks, and other domains; studies only generic LLM verifiers, not trained/fine-tuned alternatives
Insufficient statistical rigor: main results lack confidence intervals and significance testing; unclear which observed differences are meaningful; no multiple comparisons corrections

Incomplete mechanistic understanding: surface-level explanations for why patterns occur; limited investigation of problem properties causing TPR degradation; missing theoretical framework for predicting regime membership

TTS application analysis incomplete: non-standard TTS metric makes comparison to related work unclear; missing direct computational cost-benefit analysis; limited guidance on transfer to other TTS strategies

Primarily descriptive rather than prescriptive: paper characterizes what happens without developing new methods, theory, or deep mechanistic insights; limited actionable guidance for practitioners beyond testing multiple verifiers
